value.name: Aspect-is-not-fixed annotation vocabulary
value.description: Design factors, annotation layers, derived measures, and custom kinds used by the Layers release of White, Grimm, & Glass (2026). Verb senses are not defined here: they point into the PropBank ontology in the Layers repository (at://did:plc:aowbms64bhay5uiwj2w6wmy2/pub.layers.ontology.ontology/f108c4ed42756c470d4ff321).

value.name: Generality
value.gloss: Position of an event description on the generality cline (paper §2.1): contentful (specific nouns; picks out one sense), bleached (definite NPs headed by general nouns such as 'person' and 'thing'), or templatic ('X verb-PAST Y'; compatible with any sense). Called 'contentfulness' in the data files.

value.name: Concreteness
value.gloss: Whether a (sub-)sense is read concretely or abstractly; a PropBank roleset supporting both readings was split into two sub-senses (e.g. hit.01-concrete, hit.01-abstract).

value.name: Verb type
value.gloss: Manner v. result classification of a verb (paper Table 1).

value.name: Semantic class
value.gloss: Semantic field of a manner/result pair (paper Table 1).

value.name: Argument head
value.gloss: Head noun (or templatic placeholder X/Y) of a subject or object NP. Annotations carry the grammatical function as their label and the noun's number (plural) and countability (mass) as features.

value.name: Sentence pair
value.gloss: Two event descriptions sharing a verb, shown together on one Experiment 2 trial (one per line).

value.name: Calibration category
value.gloss: Target similarity band of an Experiment 2 calibration pair (pairs from Cao et al. 2024 whose normed ratings span the scale).

value.name: Telicity (in/for cloze diagnostic)
value.gloss: Measured property of Experiment 1a: the preference for completing an event description with a temporal modifier headed by 'in' v. 'for'.

value.name: Durativity (temporal-overlap diagnostic)
value.gloss: Measured property of Experiment 1b: what proportion of a temporal modifier's span the described event is judged to occupy.

value.name: Modal response share
value.gloss: Mean, over items, of the share of an item's responses that fall on its most frequent response (paper §6).

value.name: Per-sentence aspectual measures
value.gloss: Layer subkind: the three posterior-mean logits of paper §4 and the time unit each sentence was evaluated at.

value.name: Cloze in-logit
value.gloss: Posterior mean log-odds of choosing 'in' (Experiment 1a fit), for an average participant and list, at numeral 1 and the sentence's evaluation time unit, with the latent sense weights applied.

value.name: Overlap logit under 'in'
value.gloss: Posterior mean log-odds of an overlap response under 'in' (Experiment 1b fit), evaluated as for the cloze logit.

value.name: Overlap logit under 'for'
value.gloss: Posterior mean log-odds of an overlap response under 'for' (Experiment 1b fit), evaluated as for the cloze logit.

value.name: Evaluation time unit
value.gloss: Time unit at which a sentence's logits are evaluated: the mode of a Gaussian KDE over its cloze durations in log-minutes, snapped to the nearest (numeral=1, unit) duration (§4).

value.name: Per-pair measures
value.gloss: Layer subkind: aspectual match (overall and per logit) and the same-sense probability of an Experiment 2 sentence pair.

value.name: Aspectual match
value.gloss: Probability that a third sentence drawn uniformly from the other materials does not lie between the two sentences on any of the three logits, averaged over posterior draws (§4).

value.name: Aspectual match on the cloze logit alone
Aspectual match on the overlap-in logit alone
Aspectual match on the overlap-for logit alone
Same-sense probability
value.gloss: Probability that the two sentences are interpreted under the same PropBank roleset: the dot product of their sense weights (concreteness marginalized), averaged over the posterior draws of the Experiment 1b fit (§5.4).

value.name: Generality pair
value.gloss: Generality of the two members of an Experiment 2 pair.

value.name: Latent sense weight
value.gloss: Posterior weight of one (roleset, concreteness) sense in a sentence's multi-membership sense term (§2.4), per Experiment 1 fit.
